La idea de escribir la música como una l: The idea of writing music as a list and letting a machine run through it is older than electricity: the Flemish carillons of the sixteenth century carried a drum with pegs, and the music box and the pianola are the same thing. The first electronic sequencers of the 1960s (the Moog 960) were a row of eight or sixteen knobs that a clock read in a loop, exactly the list above with potentiometers. The TR-808 drum machine of 1980 and the MIDI protocol of 1983, which is the one that numbers the notes as here, turned the list into the common language of all electronic music, and the trackers of the computers of the eighties wrote songs literally as columns of numbers.

Se lee: <em>«la nota del pulso ene es el: It reads: “the note of beat n is element n modulo L of the list”, with $L$ the length of the list. And since a list of $L$ beats at $T_p$ seconds lasts $L\,T_p$ seconds, a loop of 8 quavers at 120 BPM ($T_p = 0{.}25$) lasts exactly 2 seconds: the length of the synthesiser.
